text:
mira (vp-product): quick recap from today’s all-hands — folks asked for clearer guidance on positioning vs CloudAI and EdgeServe, and how that should affect team roadmaps. can leadership outline the priority tradeoffs? cc @alex

alex (ceo): short version: mission stands — make inference predictable & economical. priorities: 1) keep hosted API as the fastest path for PLG; 2) scale Dedicated for predictable enterprise revenue; 3) keep Private for regulated customers. we should optimize for latency/cost where it helps product adoption, and for SLAs where customers pay for it. will share a one-pager by EOD.

dani (head-sales): super helpful, thanks. follow-up: for Q4 deals, is the expectation to push Dedicated first, or propose Hosted + migration path? sellers need the standard playbook.

alex (ceo): recommend: start with Hosted for trials/POCs. for accounts that need isolation/performance guarantees, move to Dedicated. Private is for legal/compliance-driven deals. sales should use the "start small, commit later" template we’ll publish.

sam (research): curious about technical differentiation callouts for doc — do we call out "unified runtime + smart routing + caching" explicitly, or keep it higher level?

alex (ceo): call out concrete differentiators: unified runtime across deployments, caching/batching unit-economics, and predictable latency SLOs. keep one short bulletsheet and one deeper product appendix.

devon (eng): on roadmap alignment: does this mean we prioritize kernel/runtime perf work over new admin features in the next sprint? want to align sprint planning.

alex (ceo): short: both matter but sequence depends on customer signal. if you have active Dedicated deals that require perf, prioritize runtime. otherwise, small admin/ops wins that unblock sales are ok. engineering leads — please flag any blockers in your weekly sync.

mira (vp-product): one more ask — can we be explicit about competitive posture? a few folks worried we sound identical to "CloudAI" on pricing and to "EdgeServe" on on-prem. do we have a short line to use in customer-facing templates?

dani (head-sales): +1. sales scripts would love a one-liner: why choose Redwood vs CloudAI/EdgeServe.

alex (ceo): proposed line: "Redwood provides a production-first inference platform that balances developer velocity with predictable performance and cost across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments." short + differentiates. feedback welcome.

sam (research): I’d add a technical parenthetical for eng slides: "high-throughput runtime + workload-aware caching and smart routing" — keeps it concrete for engineers.

dani (head-sales): love it. can marketing make two variants: one simple and one slightly technical for sales engineers?

alex (ceo): yes — marketing to produce two micro-copy variants and the one-pager. ops-bot: publishing checklist?

ops-bot: created task T-4821 in #product-ops: "Publish leadership one-pager + sales playbook + micro-copy" assigned to @mira, due in 3 business days.

mira (vp-product): thanks all — i’ll follow up with the draft and link to the doc here. if you have specific roadmap concerns that depend on a different prioritization, drop them in the product-roadmap thread or DM me. :thumbsup:
